sections.html:
Roy is a residential city in Weber County, on the west side of Interstate 15 in the Ogden-Clearfield metro area. It works as a bedroom community, with few local employers and most residents commuting out. The elevation is about 4,377 feet. Hooper lies to the west, West Haven to the north, Riverdale and Ogden to the east, and Clinton and Sunset in Davis County to the south.

Roy is not one uniform market. Older homes on the eastern bench went up mostly in the 1950s and 1960s, while newer building moved west and south after about 2005. Two houses a mile apart can differ in age, lot size and repair needs.

sections.h2: Why Roy has so many mid-century houses
sections.html:
World War II and the military sites around it drove Roy's growth. The town incorporated on March 10, 1937, and its population leapt from 868 in 1940 to 3,723 in 1950. Workers from Hill Air Force Base, the Navy Supply Depot (now the Freeport Center) and the Defense Supply Depot lived here, and entry-level homes filled the eastern bench through the 1950s and 1960s. Building continued at the western base of the hill from the 1980s.

Many Roy sellers therefore hold starter homes with original plumbing, older electrical panels, single-pane windows or an unfinished basement. A buyer with a loan often asks for repairs on those items. A cash buyer can take the house in its present condition.

Hill Air Force Base is the biggest single influence on Roy's housing demand, and its north entrance is reached from I-15 exit 338, close to Roy. A 2019 economic impact statement put the base's annual impact at $3.7 billion, with 27,650 people counted, including 5,705 military and 16,653 civilians.

Base employees sometimes have to move on a set timeline after a reassignment or a PCS order. For them, a fixed closing date can matter more than the last dollar of price.

I-15 exit 338 connects to Utah State Route 97 (5600 South), one of Roy's main roads. FrontRunner commuter rail has a Roy station that opened on April 26, 2008, with the northern segment of the line. Two sets of tracks cross the city at 2700 West, carrying FrontRunner and Union Pacific trains, so a house near that corridor may hear train noise, and a buyer or inspector may mention it.

  • Exit 338 leads to 5600 South and the Hill AFB north gate.
  • FrontRunner stops at the Roy station for trips along the Wasatch Front.
  • Freight and passenger tracks run near 2700 West.

Roofs, furnaces and water lines take a beating from cold winters and hot, dry summers. January highs average 37 degrees, July highs 94, and the record low is minus 26. About 18.4 inches of precipitation falls a year, mostly in April or May.

Repeated freezing and thawing cracks concrete, strains exposed pipes and shortens the life of asphalt shingles. If your roof is near the end of its life, a conventional buyer is likely to ask for a price cut.

Weber School District covers all of Roy, which has seven elementary schools, three junior highs and two high schools. Newer schools such as Haven Bay Elementary, Mountain View Junior High and West Field High may not appear on older lists, so confirm the school for a specific address with the district.

Roy is mostly owner-occupied. In 2020 it had 12,944 households, with 10,508 owner-occupied (81.2%) and 2,436 renter-occupied (18.8%), plus 13,346 housing units at a 3.0% vacancy rate.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit to fix up a Roy house before selling?
sections.html:
Many repairs and additions here need a permit, filed online through the city's My City Inspector portal. A plan set for a one or two family dwelling must include a site plan, a footing and foundation plan, floor plans, elevations, insulation R-values and energy compliance documents, as the city's handout lists. State law aims to finish initial plan review within 14 business days of acceptance. For fees and exempt small projects, phone the Building Official.

Many Roy sales stall on unpermitted work, since a buyer's lender or inspector may ask about a finished basement or converted garage. A cash buyer lets you skip permitting and finishing work you no longer want to pay for.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and delinquency
sections.html:
Think of the Roy tax year as a short run of dates. The county looks at your house as it stood on January 1. Late July or early August brings a valuation notice. A primary residence gets a 45 percent cut in taxable value, and that cut reaches the buildings plus the first acre of land.

Disagree with the number? You have until September 15 or 45 days after the notice, whichever runs later. Weber County hears a late case only for a death in the family, a serious medical emergency or a factual mistake in the property description.

Payment is due November 30, except when that date is a weekend or recognized holiday. Miss it and the clock changes.

  • From December 1 the account is delinquent. Pay in full by January 31 and the penalty is the greater of $10 or 1 percent.
  • Past January 31, the penalty becomes the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent, and interest is charged back to January 1.
  • A parcel delinquent for five years can be sold at tax sale.

Your title company will prorate the year's bill at closing. Ask to see the numbers before you sign.

Recording at the Weber County Recorder costs $45.00 for the first page under HB 38, with nothing extra for additional standard pages. A page larger than 8.5 by 14 inches adds $2.00, and so does each description over 10.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Roy?
sections.html:
Owners here usually weigh a traditional listing, a sale by owner and a cash sale against each other, and the three behave differently.

  • A listing reaches the most buyers but brings showings, repair requests after inspection and the possibility that a buyer's loan collapses.
  • Selling it yourself saves the agent's fee while marketing, contracts and disclosures land on you.
  • A cash sale to a company like ours closes when you say and takes the house exactly as it is. That suits inherited, tenant-occupied and neglected homes.

A house that has gone decades without maintenance deserves a cash offer request. Compare the figure with what a listing would net once repairs, carrying costs and a longer wait are subtracted. Asking costs nothing.

faqs.q: Is Roy, Utah in Weber County?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lies west of Interstate 15 in the Ogden-Clearfield metro area, and its property tax bills come from Weber County.

faqs.q: When are Roy property taxes due?
faqs.a: Each November 30, unless a weekend or holiday intervenes. From December 1 the balance is delinquent, and paying in full by January 31 costs a penalty of the greater of $10 or 1 percent.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a property valuation in Roy?
faqs.a: Whichever is later: September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed. The Weber County Board of Equalization takes the filing, and late ones need severe circumstances.

faqs.q: Does a Roy house need repairs before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No, we buy houses in their present condition. It still helps to tell us about known issues like roof leaks, an old furnace or unpermitted work.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Roy?
faqs.a: Yes, once you hold legal authority to sell, such as a personal representative or an owner on the title. A Utah attorney or title company can sort out the paperwork, and then you can ask for a cash offer if you want a quick closing.
